basis: The printing heads this block 'VERS. 3-4.' and it opens 'VERS. 3-4.-- Quasi olera virentia tradidi vobis omnia, excepto quod carnem cum sanguine'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Angelomus was a monk of Luxeuil in the middle of the ninth century and wrote for the Emperor Lothar I, who reigned from 840 to 855 and whom the verse prooemium addresses. The Genesis commentary is placed with his commentaries on Kings and on the Song of Songs in that decade. The wiki header gives the eleventh century, which is a century and a half out and is not followed. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1852 printing.
text: VERS. 3-4.-- Quasi olera virentia tradidi vobis omnia, excepto quod carnem cum sanguine non comedatis. Sanguinem enim animarum vestrarum requiram de manu cunctarum bestiarum et de manu hominis, et reliqua. Quanti enim effuderunt sanguinem, et sanguis eorum effusus non est, et alii occiderunt | hominem veneno, vel suspendio, et eorum sanguis non est effusus! Quomodo ergo Dominus effusurus est sanguinem eorum, cum illius [ Petr. illi, vel ille] qui occidit, sanguinem effuderit? Et in resurrectione ridiculum est, et in hac vita, et ideo sanguis hominis vitale [ Z., vitalis], quo vegetatur, et sustentatur, et vivit, debet intelligi; quod qui effuderit sive per scandalum, sive perversitate doctrinae, in die judicii effudetur ab eo, qui [ Petr., quod] sibi videbatur habere vitale. Caeterum, historialiter, post diluvium primum esus carnium homini conceditur, videlicet propter infecunditatem terrae, ut aestimatur, et hominis fragilitatem.
